name: Long-term memory
summary: Remembers things across conversations, and always knows the few you pin — your name, how to talk to you. Can also write things down by itself, once you turn that on.

settings.label: How much to bring back
settings.hint: How many remembered things a search returns at most. More is more context and more cost.

settings.label: Write things down by itself
settings.hint: Off, Alexia only remembers what it is told to. On, every finished exchange is kept briefly and turned into notes on a timer — nothing leaves this machine that would not have anyway, and credentials are stripped before it ever sees them.

settings.label: How often to sort through it
settings.hint: Minutes between passes. An empty buffer costs nothing — no model is called when there is nothing to sort.

settings.label: Sort through it now
settings.hint: Do the next pass now instead of waiting for the timer. Does nothing if there is nothing waiting.

settings.label: Forget everything
settings.hint: Empties long-term memory. The conversation you are having now is not touched — that belongs to Alexia, not to this plugin.

widgets.label: The shape of it
widgets.hint: Every remembered thing, and what it is filed under. Drag one to move it, scroll to zoom, click one to read the whole of it. A ring means Alexia worked that one out from something you said rather than being told it — those are the ones worth checking.

widgets.label: Remembered
widgets.hint: Everything Alexia has written down about you, whether you said it or it worked it out, and whether it is still true. What stopped being true is kept at the bottom as history; forgetting one takes every version of it.

rowActions.label: Forget
rowActions.confirm: Forget it, and every earlier version of it?
